summary: NOVA MISSION COMMAND is an interactive space mission design and simulation platform developed by NOVA TECH AFRICA. It allows users to plan and evaluate a space mission by selecting mission objectives, spacecraft configurations, launch vehicles, and scientific instruments. The simulation engine analyzes key engineering constraints, including mass capacity, power balance, mission budget, orbital parameters, and communication capabilities. Users receive mission status results, performance scores, warnings, and recommendations to help them understand the impact of their engineering decisions. By combining an accessible interface with a modular simulation engine, NOVA MISSION COMMAND makes space mission planning more engaging and educational. Our goal is to help students and beginners explore the complexity of real-world space engineering through interactive experimentation.
details:
NOVA MISSION COMMAND is an educational space mission design platform that transforms complex mission planning concepts into an interactive experience.

The application guides users through five main mission design stages: mission definition, spacecraft configuration, launch vehicle selection, scientific payload selection, and final mission review. Once the configuration is complete, the simulation engine evaluates the mission using several engineering constraints.

The system analyzes spacecraft and payload mass against launcher capacity, compares available electrical power with mission consumption, estimates mission costs, evaluates orbital parameters, and assesses communication capabilities. It then generates a mission outcome, a performance score, warnings, and recommendations.

The platform combines a web-based dashboard, an interactive mission builder, a backend API, and a modular Python simulation engine. The frontend uses Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Three.js, and Recharts. The backend uses Python, FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, Pydantic, and SQLite.

NOVA MISSION COMMAND is creative because it combines multiple mission engineering constraints into one accessible learning environment. Instead of simply presenting theoretical information, it allows users to experiment with engineering decisions and understand how those decisions influence mission feasibility and performance.

The expected impact is to encourage scientific curiosity, computational thinking, problem-solving, and interest in aerospace engineering, particularly among students and young people who want to discover space mission design.
